sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Useful commands for Basis Administrators working with Linux.

sections.heading: Send email
sections.text: To send the output of a program by email, use a pipe: | mailx -s "$(hostname) control_check_ora.log" adminsap@company.example

sections.heading: Find files
sections.text: Find files modified in the last day and format the timestamp: find /path/to/directory/* -mtime -1 | xargs ls -ldtrh --time-style="+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S" find /oracle/*/sapdata? | xargs ls -ldtrh --time-style="+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S" | grep sr3.data

sections.heading: Check ports
sections.text: nc -zv webserver.local 8080 Output: Connection to webserver.local 8080 port [tcp/*] succeeded!

sections.heading: Create a large file
sections.text: Create a 10G file: dd if=/dev/zero of=/oracle/<SID>/DELETE_IF_NECESSARY.SAP bs=1 count=0 seek=10737418240

sections.heading: Sync with remote directories using an SSH key
sections.text: Sync remote directories using rsync over SSH instead of SFTP: rsync -auvz -e "ssh -l root -i <SSH_PRIV_KEY>" <source_server>:/path/to/source/directory /local/target/path

sections.heading: Generate HTML report after upgrade
sections.text: Get all .xml and .xsl files from /usr/sap/<SID>/SUM/abap/doc (root directory only). From a Linux box, run the following commands to generate the HTML reports: xsltproc UpgAnalysis.xsl UPGANA.XML > report.html xsltproc SAPupPhaseList.xsl phaselist.xml > phaselist.html

sections.heading: Check or download certificates
sections.text: Check certificate details for a web server: curl -I https://webserver.company.example -v Inspect the full certificate chain: openssl s_client -showcerts -connect api.company.example:443 Note The commands above connect to the target host on port 443 and display the certificate chain, issuer, validity dates, and TLS session details.
